state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It seems like you may be confusing rest and movement on the distance-time graph. Let's focus on how to interpret the different sections of the graph to determine what Fido is doing at each point. Can you explain why you think Fido has fallen asleep during the negative-sloping section?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think I said that because the line goes down, so I thought Fido wasn't moving... but now I'm confused because you said it's about rest and movement. Does the downward slope mean he's actually moving back towards his home? Like, is the line going down because the distance is getting smaller?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It's great that you're considering the direction of the line on the graph. Let's explore the concept of rest and movement a bit further. Think about how the slope of the line relates to Fido's motion. What does a negative slope indicate in terms of Fido's distance from home?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly names and addresses the specific misconception about rest vs. movement, the student demonstrates clear progress by self-correcting their understanding that downward slope means returning home rather than being at rest, though the teacher's questions could have been more directive given the student's initial confusion.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher effectively scaffolds by breaking down the problem (focusing first on interpreting graph sections, then on slope meaning), adjusts support when the student shows confusion, and uses guiding questions rather than direct answers to work within the student's ZPD.
